page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Marginal notes in the right margin, beside lines 1, 2 and 6 of the column. Running head at the top, page number at the top right. Catchword and signature at the foot.

main_text.p: Corvinus ) quod sint benevola. Sed an non dam-Corvin. cont.nantur in creaturis intelligentibus cæcus & bru-Molin. e. 5. f. 6.tus amor eorum, quæ ignorant sintne affecu-turæ, an non uti Coridon ardebat Alexin (ut ait Maro) nec quid speraret habebat. Eodem modo Deus ardebit amore salutis omnium hominum & diabolorum nesciens, sitne id obtenturus. ImoIbid. sect. 7. (inquit Corvinus) non necesse est, ut Deus quando aliquid intendit ac vult, consideret sitne id obtenturus nec ne, sed sufficit ut consideret quod cum ex bonitate, tum ex amore erga iustitiam ipsum defiderare, deceat. Sed 1. naturalia Dei defideria antevertunt decreta libera & actus sapientiæ divinæ, uti cum Arminianis docet Grevincho-vius: hoc vero reforbet Corvinus & vult Deum velle & intendere salutem creaturæ ex amore erga iustitiam, & ex sua decentia uti fabulatur Corvinus. Ergo Dei decentiæ & sapientiæ actus, quibus considerat, æquum esse & iustum ut talia desideret, priores erunt voluntate antecedente at naturalia libero in Deo priora esse creditur, id quod ipsi docent. Ecce hic erit aperta contradictio. 2. Nullus appeti-tus brutinus est expers cognitionis sensitivæ in suo genere perfectissimæ: non ergo datur in Deo affectus expers cognitionis infinitæ, quæ penetret non tantum in decentiam & sapientiam desiderii sive affectus, sed etiam in desiderii impletionem. In hoc enim amor creaturæ intelligentis est imperfectus, quod non præsupponit scientiam perfectam, qua scitur, sitne illi amori satisfaciendum, nec ne. 3.

page.notes: Page is a single column with marginal notes on the right. The line "Y Omnia" at the foot is the gathering signature "Y" and the catchword "Omnia". Marginal notes "Molin, e. 5." and "f. 6." are transcribed as one note; the scan's line break between them is not certain. Paragraph breaks: no indented lines are visible, so the text is kept as one paragraph running on from the previous page. Printed spelling (e.g. "defiderare", "decentiam", "speraret") is kept as printed; only u/v and i/j were normalised. The printed "1.", "2." and "3." are inline enumerators, not headings.
